description: ExosPy supplies Python implementations of terrestrial atomic-hydrogen exosphere models and associated ultraviolet-emission calculations. It supports comparisons of density assumptions and predicted Lyman-alpha intensity. The resource is documented by NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center (metadata publisher; developer not specified). The documented physical domain is Exosphere; grid spacing, supported periods and cadence depend on this version and its chosen configuration. The documentation links Public Repository, Instant Run. A software licence and any external distribution charge are not stated. The page calls the package open source, but the precise licence must be checked at its repository before redistribution. The documented space-weather effects make it a potential environmental input for infrastructure hazard exposure and resilience simulations. It is related to platform-nasa-ccmc in this catalogue. Spatial and temporal resolution were not independently established.
